title: Best Sleep Supplements of 2026
intro_mdx_or_text: Sleep supplements are a loosely regulated market where marketing routinely outruns the evidence, and effects are almost always smaller than sleep-hygiene fundamentals or treating an underlying disorder. For this 2026 ranking we scored five widely searched products against a five-criterion methodology, weighting Safety 30% and Evidence 30% most heavily, then Cost & Value 20%, Transparency 10%, and Support 10%. We prioritized single-ingredient formulas with published human trials, real per-serving doses, and independent quality testing over proprietary blends and sub-therapeutic gummies. We deliberately include non-affiliate options so our picks aren't limited to products that pay us. None of these replace a clinician's evaluation of persistent insomnia, and several interact with sedatives, antidepressants, and blood-pressure medications. Talk to a clinician before starting any sleep supplement, especially if you are pregnant, on prescription drugs, or dealing with chronic sleep problems that last more than a few weeks.
answer_block: Our top-rated sleep supplement for 2026 is Nature Made Melatonin 3 mg, scoring 8.2/10 in our five-criterion evaluation, and it is a product Firsthand earns no commission on. Melatonin has the largest human evidence base here: a 19-trial meta-analysis of 1,683 people found it shortens time to fall asleep and modestly improves sleep quality, and Nature Made carries USP verification that independently checks label accuracy at roughly $0.08 a day. It works best for circadian problems like jet lag and shift work, not routine insomnia. Doctor's Best High Absorption Magnesium (8.0) is our best evidence-backed alternative, with trials showing about 17 minutes faster sleep onset in older adults. Combination gummies like OLLY Sleep (6.6) rank lowest because a 2023 JAMA analysis found 22 of 25 melatonin gummies were inaccurately labeled. Our rankings weight Safety and Evidence at 30% each; commissions never influence placement. Persistent insomnia deserves a clinician, not escalating doses.

faq.question: What is the best sleep supplement in 2026?
faq.answer: No supplement works for everyone. Nature Made Melatonin 3 mg scored highest in our evaluation because melatonin has the largest human evidence base and Nature Made is USP verified and inexpensive, but it helps most with circadian issues like jet lag rather than chronic insomnia. Magnesium glycinate is the best-studied alternative for general sleep quality. Effects for all of them are modest compared with treating an underlying sleep disorder.

faq.question: Is it safe to take sleep supplements every night?
faq.answer: Short-term use of melatonin, magnesium (within the 350 mg/day supplemental limit), glycine, and L-theanine is generally well tolerated in healthy adults. Long-term nightly use is less studied, and these can interact with sedatives, antidepressants, and blood-pressure medications. Melatonin's long-term safety data is limited. Talk to a clinician before nightly use, especially if you are pregnant or on prescription drugs.

faq.question: Does melatonin help with insomnia or just jet lag?
faq.answer: Melatonin most reliably shifts sleep timing for jet lag, shift work, and delayed sleep phase. For chronic insomnia, NCCIH says there is not enough strong evidence to recommend it, and clinical guidelines do not consider it a first-line insomnia treatment. Persistent insomnia deserves a clinician's evaluation rather than escalating melatonin doses.

faq.question: Do you earn money from these recommendations?
faq.answer: Some links on this page are affiliate links, and we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We also deliberately include non-affiliate options — our top pick, Nature Made Melatonin, and NOW Glycine both earn us nothing. Commissions never influence our rankings, scores, or ordering; a product that pays us can and does rank below one that doesn't.

title: Best Weight-Loss Supplements of 2026
intro_mdx_or_text: Weight-loss supplements are a crowded, heavily marketed category where confident promises rarely match the published evidence. Most branded fat burners have never been tested as finished products in a controlled trial; instead they lean on individual ingredients whose effects, where measurable at all, tend to be small and only meaningful alongside a reduced-calorie diet and exercise. We approached this list as skeptics. Rather than reward slick copy, our scoring weights Safety at 30%, Evidence at 30%, Cost and Value at 20%, Transparency at 10%, and Support at 10%. Products with proprietary blends that hide doses, thin clinical support, or aggressive auto-ship and refund terms are marked down hard. The one option here with genuinely strong randomized-trial data is not a supplement at all but an FDA-approved over-the-counter drug. Read the cons as carefully as the pros.
answer_block: Our top pick is Alli (orlistat 60 mg), the only FDA-approved over-the-counter weight-loss aid, which scores 7.5/10. It is the sole product here backed by large randomized trials: in a pooled analysis of 16 orlistat trials (over 10,000 participants), it produced roughly 2.9 kg more weight loss than placebo over a year, alongside well-documented gastrointestinal side effects. Be honest about the category, though. Most branded fat burners rely on ingredients with weak or null evidence; one systematic review of 315 randomized trials found only 16 showed a significant weight difference versus control. Among the direct-response supplements we reviewed, Transparent Labs Fat Burner (6.5) rates highest mainly for disclosing every dose, while proprietary-blend products like Java Burn (4.4) and Ikaria Lean Belly Juice (4.0) score lowest. No pill replaces diet and exercise, and any supplement here should be treated as optional, not essential.

faq.question: Do you earn money from these recommendations?
faq.answer: Yes, for some of them. Several products on this list are monetized, meaning we may earn a commission if you buy through our links; those are labeled. Our top pick, Alli (orlistat), is not monetized. Affiliate relationships never change a product's score, which is driven by our published rubric weighting safety and evidence most heavily.

faq.question: Do weight loss supplements actually work?
faq.answer: Mostly not to a degree you would notice. A systematic review of 315 randomized trials of purported weight-loss supplements found only 16 demonstrated a statistically significant weight difference versus control, and the differences ranged from about 0.3 to 4.93 kg. The one strongly evidence-backed option here is orlistat, an FDA-approved drug, not a supplement. Any product may support weight management only alongside a reduced-calorie diet and exercise.

faq.question: What is the safest weight loss supplement?
faq.answer: No supplement is risk-free, and products with undisclosed proprietary blends make safety hard to judge. Among options here, the FDA-approved OTC drug orlistat has the best-characterized safety profile, though it causes gastrointestinal side effects and carries rare warnings about liver and kidney injury. Caffeine-heavy fat burners can cause jitteriness, insomnia, and raised heart rate. Talk to a clinician before starting any product.

faq.question: Are weight loss supplements FDA approved?
faq.answer: Dietary supplements are not FDA-approved before sale; the FDA does not evaluate them for effectiveness before they reach the market. Only Alli (orlistat 60 mg) on this list is an actual FDA-approved over-the-counter drug. The branded fat burners here are marketed as dietary supplements and legally cannot claim to treat or cure any disease.

title: Top GLP-1 Weight-Loss Telehealth Providers of 2026
intro_mdx_or_text: GLP-1 telehealth pricing was rewritten in 2025-2026. The FDA declared the semaglutide shortage resolved in February 2025, the legal basis for mass-compounded copies wound down, and Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly began selling Wegovy and Zepbound direct-to-consumer, pricing that most telehealth platforms now simply pass through. This directory compares six providers that verifiably operate in July 2026, from branded-only platforms (Ro, WeightWatchers Clinic, Sesame, Hims & Hers) to programs still centered on compounded medication (Mochi Health, Noom Med). Each entry separates the membership fee from the medication cost, spells out what the fee actually buys (labs, synchronous visits, insurance coordination), and lists provider-specific red flags. Scores weight Safety 30%, Evidence 30%, Cost & Value 20%, Transparency 10%, and Support 10%. All GLP-1 medications are prescription-only and require a provider evaluation; nothing here promises a treatment outcome.
answer_block: Ro Body scores highest in our 2026 comparison at 8.4/10. Ro prescribes only FDA-approved GLP-1s and passes through manufacturer direct-pay pricing, with the Wegovy pen from $199/month and the Zepbound KwikPen at $299-$449/month, on top of a membership that costs $39 the first month and then $149/month (as low as $74/month prepaid annually), with an insurance concierge for covered patients. WeightWatchers Clinic (8.3/10) is the strongest pick when insurance coordination matters most, and Sesame (8.2/10) is the value pick, with labs included from $59-$99/month. Across the category, expect roughly $250-$600/month all-in for cash-pay branded therapy. Efficacy belongs to the medications, not the platforms: in the randomized STEP 1 trial, semaglutide 2.4 mg produced a 14.9% mean body-weight reduction over 68 weeks versus 2.4% with placebo. Every option requires an eligibility screen and a licensed clinician's prescription; approval is never guaranteed.

faq.question: Do you earn money from these recommendations?
faq.answer: Yes, partially. Ro, Sesame, and Mochi Health links on this page are affiliate links, and we may earn a commission if you sign up through them. Hims & Hers, Noom Med, and WeightWatchers Clinic earn us nothing. Rankings are set by our published methodology (Safety 30%, Evidence 30%, Cost & Value 20%, Transparency 10%, Support 10%) before monetization is considered, which is why non-partner providers appear throughout the list.

faq.question: Is compounded semaglutide still legal and safe in 2026?
faq.answer: Mass compounding was allowed only while FDA listed semaglutide and tirzepatide in shortage; those shortages were declared resolved in 2025, so pharmacies may now compound copies only for patients whose medical needs cannot be met by the approved product. Compounded GLP-1s are not FDA-reviewed for safety, effectiveness, or quality, and published case reports document 10-fold dosing errors from compounded vials. Providers still centered on compounded medication carry regulatory and supply risk.

faq.question: Will insurance cover GLP-1 weight-loss medication through telehealth?
faq.answer: Sometimes. Coverage for Wegovy and Zepbound varies widely by plan and often requires prior authorization. WeightWatchers Clinic and Ro assign insurance coordinators to pursue coverage; Sesame accepts insurance for medications (copays can be as low as $25/month). Membership or program fees themselves are almost always self-pay.

faq.question: What does GLP-1 telehealth actually cost per month in 2026?
faq.answer: Two bills: a program fee ($0-$149/month, e.g., $74/month at WeightWatchers Clinic or $59-$99/month at Sesame with labs included) plus medication (cash-pay branded GLP-1s run $149-$499/month at manufacturer direct rates; compounded programs run $99-$299/month all-in). Typical all-in cash-pay totals are roughly $250-$600/month.

faq.question: Can I get a GLP-1 prescription without seeing a doctor?
faq.answer: No. Every legitimate platform requires evaluation by a licensed clinician, and BMI-based eligibility criteria apply (generally BMI >= 30, or >= 27 with a weight-related condition). Some platforms use asynchronous questionnaires rather than video visits, which is faster but means less clinical screening, and platforms with no lab work or live visit deserve extra scrutiny.

title: Best Teeth Whitening & Oral Health Products of 2026
intro_mdx_or_text: Teeth whitening is a cosmetic bleaching problem with a well-understood chemistry: hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide oxidizes stain molecules, and concentration plus contact time drive results. Marketing, however, has outrun the evidence, so we graded every product against the peer-reviewed record rather than brand claims. Our score weights Safety 30% (peroxide concentration, sensitivity and gingival-irritation risk), Evidence 30% (published clinical data for the actual product or its active), Cost & Value 20% (price per treatment and subscription traps), Transparency 10% (clear ingredient and claim disclosure), and Support 10% (returns, guarantees, service). We prioritize products with real trial data and honest labeling, which is why a non-monetized drugstore staple can outrank pricier direct-to-consumer kits. LED gadgets and oral probiotics are held to the same bar. Prices were verified on brand and retailer sites on 2026-07-11.
answer_block: Our top pick is Crest 3D Whitestrips Professional Effects (8.5/10), the most heavily studied at-home whitener you can buy without a subscription. Peroxide strips have the strongest clinical record of any OTC format: in one randomized trial, 10% hydrogen peroxide strips produced significant whitening within a single week, and the ADA grants its Seal of Acceptance to whitening strips that meet safety and efficacy standards. Expect mild, temporary tooth sensitivity, reported in 15-78% of people across bleaching studies, which resolves after treatment stops. At roughly $45-$51 for 22 treatments (about $2 per session) with no auto-ship, it beats LED kits and boutique strips on both evidence and value. Skip products that lean on hardware or bacteria over peroxide: light activation adds little to strong gels, and a major systematic review found current evidence insufficient to recommend oral probiotics for managing dental disease. Whiten with peroxide, protect your gums, and see a dentist first.

faq.question: Do you earn money from these recommendations?
faq.answer: Some links are affiliate links, meaning we may earn a commission if you buy through them at no extra cost to you. Our top pick, Crest 3D Whitestrips Professional Effects, is not monetized, and monetized products never rank higher because they pay us. Scores come only from published evidence, safety data, price and transparency.

faq.question: What is the best over-the-counter teeth whitening product?
faq.answer: For most people, hydrogen-peroxide whitening strips are the best-evidenced OTC option. They deliver measurable color change in clinical trials and are inexpensive per treatment. Whitening toothpaste helps with surface stains but changes tooth color far less than a peroxide strip or gel.

faq.question: Do led teeth whitening lights actually work?
faq.answer: The light itself does little. A systematic review and meta-analysis of in-office bleaching found no meaningful efficacy benefit from light activation with high-concentration peroxide, while light raised the odds of tooth sensitivity roughly 3.5-fold. The peroxide gel does the whitening; the LED is largely for show.

faq.question: Does teeth whitening damage enamel?
faq.answer: Used as directed, peroxide whiteners have not been shown to permanently damage enamel, but they commonly cause temporary tooth sensitivity and can irritate gums on contact. The ADA advises talking to a dentist before whitening, especially if you have restorations, gum recession or untreated decay.
